decisive_items: induced sputum was trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert and subsequently grew MTB sensitive to rifampicin and isoniazid
Biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus
MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression
response.rationale: Confirmed MTB on culture plus necrotizing AFB-positive granuloma and spinal/epidural involvement indicate disseminated tuberculosis; pulmonary TB is a component, while Pott's disease, renal TB, and CKD are narrower or unsupported alternatives.

rejected.why: Pulmonary tuberculosis is confirmed but cannot explain the extrapulmonary spine and toe lesions; it is a component of disseminated TB rather than the full diagnosis.
Pott's disease is supported by spinal MRI but represents only one manifestation; it misses pulmonary and cutaneous involvement.
Abnormal urine sediment and increased renal echogenicity are present, but there is no evidence of primary chronic kidney disease independent of the tuberculous infection.
Renal tuberculosis is plausible from the urine findings, but urine culture had no growth and there is no mycobacterial confirmation in the urine; systemic TB better explains the case.
